## Welcome ☕

This lab is meant to utilize your GIS skills for an entrepreneurial endeavor; where to open your first coffee shop. You will go through each step of the lab building a case for why your chosen location is one worth investing in. Your assignment is to create a new qmd called coffee_shop.qmd, run all the analyses outlined in this document, and render the qmd into a .html that is pushed to github for final submission on canvas. This is **due November 17th at 11:30 AM**.

### Step 3 - Map the competition

Use code like this to grab osm data on cafes in the area of your choosing. Map it and show competition relative to your chosen location, Is there tough competition around your chosen location? If so, how will your coffee shop differ? (***6 points***)

`library(osmdata)`

`oahu_bb <- c(xmin = -158.30, ymin = 21.24, xmax = -157.63, ymax = 21.73)`

`cafe_query <- opq(bbox = oahu_bb, timeout = 180) |> add_osm_features(features = list("amenity" = "cafe", "shop" = "coffee"))`

`osm_raw <- osmdata_sf(cafe_query)`

`cafe_points <- as.data.frame(osm_raw$osm_points)`

## Code that follows example

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(osmdata)
library(dplyr)
library(leaflet)
library(sf)

oahu_bb <- c(xmin = -158.30, ymin = 21.24, xmax = -157.63, ymax = 21.73)

cafe_query <- opq(bbox = oahu_bb, timeout = 180) %>%
  add_osm_features(features = list("amenity" = "cafe", "shop" = "coffee"))

osm_raw <- osmdata_sf(cafe_query)

cafe_points <- as.data.frame(osm_raw$osm_points)

cafe_map <- st_as_sf(cafe_points) %>%
  filter(!is.na(name))

leaflet() %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(data = cafe_map, radius = 5, color = "brown", label = cafe_map$name) %>%
  addMarkers(lng = -157.8454, lat = 21.3014, label = "HAYN Coffee") %>%
  setView(lng = -157.8454, lat = 21.3014, zoom = 15)
```

## I had to try a different way to view potential coffee shop competitors. The sample code above wouldn't load, so instead of using the osmdata from the live server, I used the osmextract package to download an osm file. I filtered the data to show cafes or shops, however my shop shows limited competition within walking distance, but heavier competition for customers with transportation access.

## My map shows the bulk of my competition is near Ala Moana. My hope is that our coffee shop is near a lot of the thrifting stores (Harbor's Vintage, Goodwill and Plato's Closet) and can attract some of the younger crowd. Being away from Ala Moana will also give us an edge with pricing and affordability will be our selling point.

```{r}

library(osmextract)
library(dplyr)
library(leaflet)

hawaii_points <- oe_get("Hawaii", layer = "points", extra_tags = c("amenity", "shop"))

cafe_points <- hawaii_points %>%
  filter(amenity == "cafe" | shop == "coffee", !is.na(name))

leaflet() %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(data = cafe_points, radius = 5, color = "brown", label = cafe_points$name) %>%
  addMarkers(lng = -157.8454, lat = 21.3014, label = "HAYN Coffee") %>%
  setView(lng = -157.8454, lat = 21.3014, zoom = 15)
```

### Step 4.1 - Resident Customer Demographics

How can we map some spatial information describing your potential customers. Use `tidycensus` to pull in some census data for the tract your coffee shop is in.

Within the get_acs() function think of putting in some of these variable codes based on what is most relevant to your coffee shop (***4 points***)

| Code | Name in script | What it measures | Universe (denominator) |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| B01001_001 | `total_pop` | Total population | All residents |
| B01001_007 | `m_18_19` | Male, 18–19 years | All residents |
| B01001_008 | `m_20` | Male, 20 years | All residents |
| B01001_009 | `m_21` | Male, 21 years | All residents |
| B01001_010 | `m_22_24` | Male, 22–24 years | All residents |
| B01001_011 | `m_25_29` | Male, 25–29 years | All residents |
| B01001_012 | `m_30_34` | Male, 30–34 years | All residents |
| B01001_031 | `f_18_19` | Female, 18–19 years | All residents |
| B01001_032 | `f_20` | Female, 20 years | All residents |
| B01001_033 | `f_21` | Female, 21 years | All residents |
| B01001_034 | `f_22_24` | Female, 22–24 years | All residents |
| B01001_035 | `f_25_29` | Female, 25–29 years | All residents |
| B01001_036 | `f_30_34` | Female, 30–34 years | All residents |
| B19013_001 | `med_hh_income` | Median household income (inflation-adjusted dollars) | Households |
| B08301_001 | `commuters` | Total workers 16+ (base for commute shares) | Workers 16+ |
| B08301_010 | `transit` | Commute by public transportation (excl. taxi) | Workers 16+ |
| B08301_018 | `bike` | Commute by bicycle | Workers 16+ |
| B08301_019 | `walk` | Walked to work | Workers 16+ |
| B08301_021 | `wfh` | Worked from home | Workers 16+ |
| B14001_001 | `school_pop` | Population 3+ (base for enrollment) | Population 3+ |
| B14001_008 | `college_ug` | Enrolled in college, undergraduate | Population 3+ |
| B14001_009 | `college_grad` | Enrolled in graduate or professional school | Population 3+ |
| B15003_001 | `pop_25plus` | Population 25+ (base for education) | Population 25+ |
| B15003_022 | `bachelors` | Bachelor’s degree | Population 25+ |
| B15003_023 | `masters` | Master’s degree | Population 25+ |
| B15003_024 | `professional` | Professional school degree (JD, MD, etc.) | Population 25+ |
| B15003_025 | `doctorate` | Doctorate degree | Population 25+ |
| B25064_001 | `med_gross_rent` | Median gross rent (residential, rent + utilities) | Renter-occupied units paying cash rent |

As mentioned earlier, I would focus on reaching a younger crowd, making the selling point of the shop affordability. I decided to display census tract data by our target audience(ages 18-30) and median household rent This gave me a better idea of how well our location fit our marketing strategy.

```{r}
library(tidycensus)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(leaflet)

hnl_tracts <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  state = "HI",
  county = "Honolulu",
  year = 2023,
  variables = c(total_pop = "B01001_001",
                med_gross_rent = "B25064_001",
                m_18_19 = "B01001_007",
                m_20 = "B01001_008",
                m_21 = "B01001_009",
                m_22_24 = "B01001_010",
                m_25_29 = "B01001_011",
                f_18_19 = "B01001_031",
                f_20 = "B01001_032",
                f_21 = "B01001_033",
                f_22_24 = "B01001_034",
                f_25_29 = "B01001_035"),
  output = "wide",
  geometry = TRUE
)

hnl_tracts <- hnl_tracts %>%
  mutate(young_pct = (m_18_19E + m_20E + m_21E + m_22_24E + m_25_29E +
                      f_18_19E + f_20E + f_21E + f_22_24E + f_25_29E) / total_popE * 100) %>%
  st_transform(4326)

shop_tract <- hnl_tracts %>%
  filter(GEOID == "15003003501")

data.frame(tract = shop_tract$NAME,
           population = shop_tract$total_popE,
           pct_18_29 = round(shop_tract$young_pct, 1),
           median_rent = shop_tract$med_gross_rentE)
pal <- colorNumeric("YlOrBr", hnl_tracts$young_pct)

leaflet(hnl_tracts) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addPolygons(fillColor = pal(hnl_tracts$young_pct), fillOpacity = 0.7, color = "white", weight = 1,
              label = paste0(hnl_tracts$NAME, ": ", round(hnl_tracts$young_pct, 1),
                             "% ages 18-29, median rent $", hnl_tracts$med_gross_rentE)) %>%
  addPolygons(data = shop_tract, fill = FALSE, color = "red", weight = 3) %>%
  addMarkers(lng = -157.8454, lat = 21.3014, label = "HAYN Coffee") %>%
  addLegend(pal = pal, values = hnl_tracts$young_pct, title = "% ages 18-29") %>%
  setView(lng = -157.8454, lat = 21.3014, zoom = 14)
```

### Step 4.2 - Working Customer Demographics

Utilizing [LODES data](https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/) and the l[ehdr package](https://github.com/jamgreen/lehdr/) make some maps describing workforce characteristics of the tract around your shop (***4 points)***

```{r}
library(lehdr)

hi_wac <- grab_lodes(state = "hi", year = 2022, lodes_type = "wac",
                     job_type = "JT00", segment = "S000", agg_geo = "tract")

hnl_jobs <- hnl_tracts %>%
  left_join(hi_wac, by = c("GEOID" = "w_tract")) %>%
  mutate(high_earn_pct = CE03 / C000 * 100)

pal_jobs <- colorNumeric("Blues", hnl_jobs$C000)

leaflet(hnl_jobs) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addPolygons(fillColor = pal_jobs(hnl_jobs$C000), fillOpacity = 0.7, color = "white", weight = 1,
              label = paste0(hnl_jobs$NAME, ": ", hnl_jobs$C000, " jobs, ",
                             round(hnl_jobs$high_earn_pct, 1), "% earn over $3,333/mo")) %>%
  addPolygons(data = shop_tract, fill = FALSE, color = "red", weight = 3) %>%
  addMarkers(lng = -157.8454, lat = 21.3014, label = "HAYN Coffee") %>%
  addLegend(pal = pal_jobs, values = hnl_jobs$C000, title = "Total jobs") %>%
  setView(lng = -157.8454, lat = 21.3014, zoom = 14)
```

### Step 5 - What's nearby?

Utilizing [isochrones](https://walker-data.com/posts/accessibility-surface/) show us whats a 5 minute drive and 10 minute walk from your shop. Think about utilizing rush hour traffic data when people would grab a coffee before work (if that is your audience/customer base) (***4 points)***

Within a 10 minute walking distance, there are only 2 other coffee spots, granted one is Starbucks which could present some issues competitively, but other than that we have a great location for those who commute on foot. Zooming out, there is a greater threat of competition for driving customers. The bulk of the competition is located closer to Ala Moana. Our location is a great middle point for those getting off the Kinau exit and heading into town, or those traveling from the east to downtown.

```{r}
library(mapboxapi)

drive_5 <- mb_isochrone(location = c(-157.8454, 21.3014), profile = "driving-traffic",
                        time = 5, depart_at = "2026-12-02T07:30")

walk_10 <- mb_isochrone(location = c(-157.8454, 21.3014), profile = "walking", time = 10)

leaflet() %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addPolygons(data = drive_5, color = "blue", fillOpacity = 0.2, label = "5-min drive (7:30 AM traffic)") %>%
  addPolygons(data = walk_10, color = "darkgreen", fillOpacity = 0.4, label = "10-min walk") %>%
  addCircleMarkers(data = cafe_points, radius = 5, color = "brown", label = cafe_points$name) %>%
  addMarkers(lng = -157.8454, lat = 21.3014, label = "HAYN Coffee") %>%
  addLegend(colors = c("blue", "darkgreen"), labels = c("5-min drive", "10-min walk"))
```

### Step 6 - Do you need a generator?

At the county level, use the [eagle i dataset](https://www.osti.gov/biblio/3012826) to show how many times the county your coffee shop is in lost power in 2025. Make a line plot of outages over time with `ggplot` (***3 points***)

While there was an outage nearly every day of the year, most of the outages were a very small fraction of the Honolulu county population. I dont think that there's any indication of power outages being a frequent problem for our shop. That being said, outages do still happen, and it would likely be a good idea to invest in a backup generator.

```{r}
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(arrow)
library(here)

outages <- read_feather(here("data/hawaii_outages_2025.feather"))

hnl_daily <- outages %>%
  filter(state == "Hawaii", county == "Honolulu") %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(run_start_time)) %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(max_out = max(customers_out))

nrow(hnl_daily)

ggplot(hnl_daily, aes(x = date, y = max_out)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Honolulu County power outages, 2025",
       x = "Date", y = "Max customers without power")
```

### Step 7 - Conclusion

Write a 7-12 sentence summary on why you think your cafe location is a good choice/worth investing in based on the spatial data you were able to describe in the steps above. (***6 points***)

I believe that the Pensacola location chosen for HAYN Coffee has great potential and is worth investing in. One of the location's greatest strengths is the limited walk-in competition. As shown by the isochrone graph, there are only 2 other coffee shops within a 10 minute walking distance. While Starbucks is a strong competitor, our shop being a locally-owned business with an aggresive marketing strategy for our designated clientele gives us a great edge to be the top pick in the immediate area.

If we are solely basing the potential for this business on location data and the graphs created for this assignment, there is a lot left to be desired. As shown by our resident customer demographics, there are locations on the island much better suited for a business targeting patrons age (18-30). The average median household rent per tract is also fairly distributed. In a perfect world, the rents per tract surrounding our shop would be closer so we could better understand our market and price accordingly. I still believe in the location of our business for reasons outside of the graphs created in this qmd.
